title: Video Swin Transformer
layout_note: A single row: 'Videos' box, a tall '3D Patch Partition' bar, then four dashed rounded stage containers each holding a tall narrow bar (Linear Embedding or Patch Merging) and a big rounded 'Video Swin Transformer Block' box with a ×N repeat count under it; tensor shapes are written above each stage boundary.
grouping: Each stage is a dashed rounded rectangle titled 'Stage 1'..'Stage 4' at its top edge, with the repeat count (×2, ×2, ×6, ×2) at its bottom edge; nothing else is grouped and there is no colour.
shapes_depth: Flat black-outlined rounded rectangles on white: tall narrow bars with vertically rotated text for embedding / merging layers and large square-ish boxes with three-line centred text for the transformer blocks. Black straight arrows; no fill, shading or shadows.
proposed_highlight: No highlight: the paper's block is named 'Video Swin Transformer Block' in every stage and stands out only by being the largest box in each dashed container.
lesson: Write the tensor shape (T/2 × H/4 × W/4 × C …) above each stage boundary and the repeat count (×N) under each dashed stage frame, so a hierarchical backbone's scale schedule is read along one line.
notes: venue = arXiv (remembered venue: CVPR 2022; not printed on the arXiv first page); year = arXiv preprint year. The 3D shifted-window mechanism is drawn separately in Fig. 3; this overview shows only the stage layout.

arrangement.units: four dashed rounded containers in a row, one per stage, each holding a narrow embedding/merging bar and a large transformer-block box, with the stage name on the top border and ×N on the bottom border
arrangement.inputs_as: a plain box labelled 'Videos' with the input shape T×H×W×3 written above it

core.what: one left-to-right row of four dashed rounded stage containers, each a narrow Linear Embedding or Patch Merging bar followed by a large Video Swin Transformer Block box with its repeat count under it

relations.form: Videos box -> tall 3D Patch Partition bar -> Stage 1 -> Stage 2 -> Stage 3 -> Stage 4, single arrows on one horizontal line
block repetition written as x2, x2, x6, x2 under each stage container rather than drawn

channels.colour: none: black outline on white throughout
channels.shape: tall narrow bars = token reshaping (partition, embedding, merging), large rounded boxes = transformer blocks, a plain rectangle = the input
channels.line: solid black arrows for data flow
channels.frame: dashed rounded frames = one stage; tensor shapes are written above each stage boundary

quality.strengths: Arrows run on one straight line through every stage; the repeated stage unit is drawn identically four times; tensor shapes above the boundaries show the resolution pyramid; the transformer block is the largest box in each stage.
quality.weaknesses: No data is drawn (the video is a box labelled Videos, tokens are not shown), so the 3D shifted-window idea, the contribution, is invisible here; the four stages are identical boxes and only text says they differ; no colour or emphasis marks what is new versus Swin.

insights.structure: One row of four dashed rounded stage containers after a Videos box and a tall patch-partition bar, each container holding a narrow down-sampling bar and a large transformer-block box.
insights.data: No data is drawn: the input is a 'Videos' text box and every intermediate is a typeset tensor shape (T/2×H/8×W/8×2C …) above the stage boundaries.
insights.emphasis: Only size separates the method's block from the plumbing: the Video Swin Transformer Block box is the largest shape in every stage, all in plain black outline.
insights.flow: Strictly left to right on one horizontal centreline, with straight arrows crossing the dashed container borders between stages.
insights.avoid: Monochrome boxes-only rendering hides what is new (the 3D shifted window), and the inter-stage arrows run straight through the dashed borders so the frames and arrows tangle at each crossing.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
